questions.q: What did the prophet see when he lifted up his eyes?
questions.a: He saw a man with a measuring line in his hand.

questions.q: What was the young man going to do with the measuring line in his hand?
questions.a: He was going to measure Jerusalem, to determine its width and its length.

questions.q: Who came out to meet the angel who was speaking with the prophet?
questions.a: Another angel came out to meet him.

questions.q: Why did the second angel say that Jerusalem would sit in the open country?
questions.a: The second angel said this because of the multitudes of men and beasts that would be within her.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would become for Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would become a wall of fire around her and he would be the glory in her midst.

questions.q: From where did Yahweh tell the people to flee?
questions.a: Yahweh told them to flee from Babylon, because he had scattered them everywhere.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell the people living in Babylon to do?
questions.a: Yahweh told them to escape from Babylon.

questions.q: According to Yahweh, what happens to anyone who harms his people?
questions.a: Anyone who harms them harms what is most precious to Yahweh.

questions.q: How were they supposed to know that Yahweh of Armies had sent the second angel?
questions.a: They would know that Yahweh of Armies had sent him when he waved his hand over the nations that had plundered Judah and Israel, and those nations would become plunder for their own slaves.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell the people of Zion to do?
questions.a: Yahweh told them to sing and rejoice, because he was coming to live among them.

questions.q: What will happen when Yahweh comes to live among his people?
questions.a: Many nations will join themselves to Yahweh, and they will become his people.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do with Judah?
questions.a: Yahweh will claim Judah as his own special people in his holy land, and he will again choose Jerusalem.

questions.q: Why is all flesh told to be silent before Yahweh?
questions.a: All flesh is told to be silent before Yahweh because Yahweh has been roused from out of the heavens.

commentary.text: The Jews called to return to their own land.

Verses 1–5 The Son of David, even the Man Christ Jesus, whom the prophet sees with a measuring line in his hand, is the Master-Builder of his church. God notices the extent of his church, and will take care that whatever number of guests are brought to the wedding-supper, there shall be room. This vision means well to Jerusalem. The walls of a city, as they defend it, so they straiten its inhabitants; but Jerusalem shall be extended as freely as if it had no walls at all, yet shall be as safe as if it had the strongest walls. In the church of God there yet is room for other multitudes, more than man can number. None shall be refused who trust in Christ; and He never shuts out from heaven one true member of the church on earth. God will be a Wall of fire round them, which can neither be broken through nor undermined, nor can it be assailed without danger to those who attack. This vision was to have its full accomplishment in the gospel church, which is extended by admitting the Gentiles into it; and which has the Son of God for its Prince and Protector; especially in the glorious times yet to come.

If God will build Jerusalem for the people and their comfort, they must inhabit it for him and his glory. The promises and privileges with which God's people are blessed, should engage us to join them, whatever it costs us. When Zion is enlarged to make room for all God's Israel, it is the greatest madness for any of them to stay in Babylon. The captivity of a sinful state is by no means to be continued in, though a man may be easy in worldly matters. Escape for thy life, look not behind thee. Christ has proclaimed that deliverance to the captives, which he has himself wrought out, and it concerns every one to resolve that sin shall not have dominion over him. Those who would be found among God's children, must save themselves from this world, see Ac 2:40. What Christ will do for his church, shall be an evident proof of God's care and affection. He that touches you, touches the apple of his eye. This is a strong expression of God's love to his church. He takes what is done against her as done against the tenderest part of the eye, to which the least touch is a great offence. Christ is sent to be the Protector of his church.

Here is a prediction of the coming of Christ in human nature. Many nations in that day would renounce idolatry, and God will own those for his people who join him with purpose of heart. Glorious times are foretold as a prophecy of our Lord's coming and kingdom. God is about to do something unexpected, and very surprising, and to plead his people's cause, which had long seemed neglected. Silently submit to his holy will, and patiently wait the event; assured that God will complete all his work. He will ere long come to judgment, to complete the salvation of his people, and to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their sins.
